insight.title: Why Tiny Friction Points Kill Huge Business Strategies
insight.subtitle: How a single extra click can redirect billions in revenue

sections.text: Why do giants fall? It often boils down to "Friction Gravity." Small, ignored barriers don't just slow users down—they eventually pull the entire market toward a smoother, more efficient alternative.

We suffer from "Linearity Bias," assuming small hurdles don't matter. When a task is 1% easier elsewhere, tiny preferences compound until they trigger a sudden, irreversible shift in where the world spends its money.

Tomorrow's leaders don't just predict the future; they identify current friction points. By removing a single step, they create a gravity well that inevitably drains customers and revenue from the slow-moving status quo.
Try this today: When you notice a small inconvenience today, ask how removing it would change your industry.
Competitive advantage is often just the sum of all the small frustrations you refused to ignore.
